html:
A Germanic people of central Germany whose kingdom the Franks conquered in 531. The map shows them in 500, in the lands between the Harz mountains and the Main.

The Thuringii first appear in Roman writing around 400. In the late 5th and early 6th centuries their kings ruled a large kingdom and married into other royal houses: King Hermanfrid's wife was a niece of Theodoric the Great, king of the Ostrogoths. In 531 the Frankish kings Theuderic I and Chlothar I, with Saxon allies, defeated Hermanfrid and took his kingdom into the Frankish realm.

Among the captives was the young princess Radegund. Chlothar married her, but she left him and founded a convent at Poitiers, and she became one of the best known saints of Merovingian Gaul. The Saxons took the northern part of the Thuringian lands. The name lives on in the German state of Thuringia. To the south lived the Alemanni.
